public_comment.topic: Disclosure of appearance of conflict of interest due to former spouse's employment with the schools; noted this was the speaker's third or fourth such disclosure.
Presented a citizens petition warrant article to fund reinstatement of cut middle and other school sports and transportation, with a cost model built from public records.
Proposed draft operating protocols for the Finance Committee, requested to be placed on a future agenda for discussion.

votes.motion: Appoint Tom Gray as the Finance Committee's representative to the capital plan committee for a three-year term.

budget_items.topic: Transportation cost to reinstate cut sports
budget_items.what_was_said: Petitioner's model estimated round-trip transportation costs for games for all currently-cut sports including cheer for the upcoming season.
Direct cost to reinstate all cut middle school sports plus golf, skiing and women's lacrosse, per the petitioner's spreadsheet model.

budget_items.topic: Citizens petition warrant article total ask
budget_items.what_was_said: Total requested from certified free cash or other available funds to reinstate sports and transportation; a member later suggested the number may need to be reduced on the town meeting floor.

budget_items.topic: Athlete/participation counts used in the model
budget_items.what_was_said: Petitioner's model counted sport 'slots' rather than individual students; a school committee member present disputed this as roughly double the real headcount of participating students.

budget_items.topic: Allocated athletic department overhead per sport
budget_items.what_was_said: Shared costs (AD, training, Hudl licenses) are divided by season and sport count; cut sports were already absorbing a share of this overhead in the current budget.
A family with three sport participations pays per-sport fees; middle school track participants each paid a fee with almost no expenses beyond transportation.
The town began FY26 town meeting with a free cash balance allocated to savings, one-time articles, the snow and ice deficit, and the capital plan, leaving a remainder carrying into FY27 free cash.
A new state supplemental bill funds a snow/ice recovery program; Lunenburg's share is distributed by road mileage and the town does not qualify for the extraordinary-hardship portion.

budget_items.topic: FY26 snow and ice budget vs. actuals
budget_items.what_was_said: The snow and ice line was significantly overspent; the finance director compared the FY26 budgeted amount to recent years' actual expenditures.
Free cash covered part of the deficit at the May 2026 town meeting; the remainder was to be resolved by a year-end transfer until WRAP funding was announced.
Discussed as a possible but likely inapplicable funding source for the petition article, since the need appears foreseeable rather than an emergency.

budget_items.topic: FY23 capital plan — records retention project
budget_items.what_was_said: Funding for a records retention project was narrowly scoped as presented to town meeting; the basis for the estimate could not be located and the project may need to return to capital planning.

budget_items.topic: FY23 capital — public safety building engineering design
budget_items.what_was_said: Remaining design funding for moisture and drainage engineering could be reappropriated to a future project or the rest of the FY23 capital plan.

budget_items.topic: FY23 capital — senior center HVAC and town hall repairs
budget_items.what_was_said: A building code change requires the senior center HVAC project to be rescoped with insufficient remaining funds; town hall repair funding's scope (interior vs. mechanical/furnace work) is unclear.

budget_items.topic: FY23 capital — primary school classroom AC
budget_items.what_was_said: The project appears overexpended, likely due to misapplication of Green Communities and utility incentive funds that needs reconciling.

budget_items.topic: FY24/FY25 capital plan — various small remaining balances
budget_items.what_was_said: Numerous FY24-FY25 capital projects are complete with small remaining balances, including public safety radio, Turkey Hill fire system, security upgrades, court resurfacing, safety film, police vehicles, library cameras, and the Northfield Culvert/Kelly's Pond project still in design.
Proposed 1.0 reading specialist position, partially funded through anticipated FY27 health insurance savings contingency.
52 revolving one-on-one online tutoring seats proposed, potentially funded by a pending grant; described as a one-time, non-recurring expenditure.
Proposed new 1.0 reading specialist position, replacing a split 0.5/0.5 role that could not adequately serve either function.

budget_items.topic: High school assistant principal FTE increase
budget_items.what_was_said: Proposal to expand the role from 0.5 to 1.0 FTE, citing a climate/culture survey and the failed combination of assistant principal and athletic director duties.

budget_items.topic: High school music teacher FTE increase
budget_items.what_was_said: Proposal to increase a music teacher's position toward 1.0 FTE to ease scheduling and physical education requirement conflicts.
Proposed new position, previously lost to attrition and not in the current budget, sought due to rising caseloads and new state mandates limiting cool-down space use.
A new health insurance program is showing significant savings versus budget across town and school active employees, excluding retirees on active plans.

budget_items.topic: FY27 school budget request vs. level services
budget_items.what_was_said: A member recapped that schools had sought about $1.6 million to maintain FY26 level service including prior free cash use, and debated how the new state aid (roughly $400-600K) compares to that gap.
Federal Title I allocation for at-risk students came in higher than initially feared, to fund targeted instructional coaching.
Funds primarily go to a state-mandated mentoring program, with a small remainder for MAP professional development.
Safe and healthy students funding supports trauma-informed practices and clinical consultation, relatively flat year over year.
Lunenburg's share of a consortium grant for English language acquisition, funding a data platform, conference attendance, and supplies.
Entitlement grant supporting out-of-district tuitions, IEP accommodations, and staff professional development.
Smaller entitlement grant targeted to paraprofessional staffing support in the preschool program, not covering a full salary.
Newly awarded grant to implement a consistent preschool curriculum focused on closing early literacy gaps; about 42% of K-3 students are reported below benchmark.

Legislative earmark for school infrastructure with no finalized spending plan; possible uses discussed include ADA accessibility, auditorium lighting/sound, and curtain flame-retardant compliance; a member pushed for track and field design funding.
Current balance and FY27 expenditures to date were reported, funded by user fees and gate receipts; not considered a source for the citizens petition article.
Finance director broke down town revenue sources: property taxes, state aid, local receipts, and free cash/available funds.

budget_items.topic: State aid collections / Smart Growth shortfall
budget_items.what_was_said: State aid collections lagged partly because an anticipated Smart Growth payment has not been received, echoing a prior shortfall years earlier.
Local receipts came in well over budget, driven by investment income and motor vehicle excise, attributed to broader economic conditions.
Water enterprise fund figures reported, with reconciliation still underway for regional billing with the City of Fitchburg.
Budget, net expenditures after encumbrances, and revenue collected were reported for this fund.
Sewer fund revenues exceeded net expenditures once encumbrances were removed, attributed to improved collections management.
The fund is drawing down reserves as collected revenue falls well short of projections, reflecting cord-cutting trends.
Town meeting voted to create this account but it has not yet been funded; expected to appear on the funds list with a zero balance.
Committee members were surprised to find a substantial playground fund balance that grew slightly this year, likely from interest.

transfers.description: Free cash transfer to offset the FY26 snow and ice deficit, Article 9, May 2, 2026 town meeting
FY26 free cash transferred to savings/stabilization, one-time articles, and the capital plan
WRAP reimbursement (~$228,000) — either placed in a restricted special revenue fund or closed out to free cash
transfers.outcome: discussed only; pending select board decision August 18

transfers.description: Prior year unexpended capital used as an available funding source at the November 2025 town meeting (precedent example)

decisions.decision: Chair asked the school committee to meet (tentatively August 26) before the August 27 public hearing to take up and discuss the citizens petition article.
Agreement that the petitioner should be connected with the town manager, select board, and town counsel to work out the article's funding mechanism correctly.
Town manager will circulate town counsel's written opinion on the scope of 'other available funds' to the finance committee, select board, and superintendent.
The select board will decide at its August 18 meeting whether WRAP funds go into a restricted special revenue fund or close out to free cash.
Finance director will follow up with DLS on two outstanding WRAP-fund questions before the August 18 select board meeting.
Consensus that the Finance Committee Reserve Fund likely does not qualify as a funding source for the petition article since the need appears foreseeable.
Superintendent agreed that if the pending Ignite tutoring grant is awarded, the school department will inform the finance department how those funds will be used.
Adjusting mid-year revenue projections and possibly creating a dedicated fund for projected revenue overages was added as a future agenda topic.
Draft Finance Committee operating protocols will be placed on a future agenda for committee discussion and comment.
Next finance committee meeting/public hearing set for August 27.

minutes.summary: The Finance Committee heard a resident-led cost model for a citizens petition warrant article to restore cut school sports and transportation, reviewed free cash and the new state WRAP snow-and-ice reimbursement as possible funding sources (with no free cash currently available), and received the town manager's first capital/outstanding-articles report. The superintendent presented a research-based plan for spending anticipated additional state aid on literacy staffing and behavioral support rather than general class-size reduction, prompting extended debate about messaging versus prior budget cuts; the meeting closed with a Q3 FY26 financial report, a special revenue funds review, and the appointment of Tom Gray to the capital planning committee.
